output.why: A has the most restraint and the best ending. It opens on the piano, lets the clockwork (the repeater's 10:38, the regulator set back to 10:05, the hall clock striking eleven) work without comment, and closes on "I have no more to add" and the line about Félix, which carries real feeling without asking for it. Its one weakness is the watch: a watch two minutes fast turns a 10:45 claim into 10:43, which still falls after the strike, so the correction does no work in the alibi. F is the cleanest mechanism. It admits the single lie without the watch detail and adds "A house of this kind keeps its own time," and it ends on "tell her that the choice was mine alone," which lands harder than most endings here. C has the best image in the set, "a repeater cannot be made to unsay what it has said," and a quiet close with "I shall not need to be fetched." The Primum non nocere grammar joke is a little precious. E has good moments ("I find I mean it too"), but its last lines move into moral instruction and a cute tag about the watch. D is clear and dry, with a useful "history rather than opinion" stance, but the timestamp ledger and the explicit list of what he did not reckon with explain the clockwork to the reader. Its ending, "Please tell Odile before the others do," is good. B lectures most. It spells out every step, sermonises on Tempora mutantur and on Félix's motives, and polishes its own neatness ("a careful physician... a worse one to be found out as"). It is the least believable voice, because a man in this position would not pause to be quotable.
